prompt: Which display has bars drawn over **numerical intervals** with no gaps: a bar graph or a histogram?
hint: One of these displays compares separate categories such as favourite colours. The other groups numbers into ranges.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Use a sample of 3–4 values to see how the rule works, then apply it to the real data.
One of these displays compares separate categories such as favourite colours. The other groups numbers into ranges.
Numerical intervals such as $0$-$9$ and $10$-$19$ follow each other on a number line, so their bars touch. Category bars are drawn apart.
The display with touching bars over numerical intervals is the histogram.

explanation: A bar graph compares separate categories, and its bars are drawn with gaps between them.
A histogram groups numerical data into intervals that follow one another on a number line.
Because the intervals join up, the bars touch, so the display described is a histogram.
